location: Chapter 6, Bahia Blanca to Buenos Ayres
location_zh: 第 6 章《从巴伊亚布兰卡到布宜诺斯艾利斯》
text_en: The city of Buenos Ayres is large; and I should think one of the most regular in the world. Every street is at right angles to the one it crosses, and the parallel ones being equidistant, the houses are collected into solid squares of equal dimensions, which are called quadras. On the other hand, the houses themselves are hollow squares; all the rooms opening into a neat little courtyard. … In the centre of the town is the Plaza, where the public offices, fortress, cathedral, etc., stand. Here also, the old viceroys, before the revolution, had their palaces.
text_zh: 布宜诺斯艾利斯城很大，我想它是世界上最规整的城市之一。每条街都和与它相交的街成直角，平行的街道间距相等，于是房屋聚成一个个大小相同的实心方块，叫作“夸德拉”。另一方面，房子本身却是空心的方块，所有房间都朝着一个整洁的小院子开门。……城中央是广场，政府机关、要塞、大教堂等都在这里。革命以前，旧日的总督们也在这里建有宫殿。

location_zh: 第 5 章《巴伊亚布兰卡》
text_en: At Punta Alta we have a section of one of these later-formed little plains, which is highly interesting from the number and extraordinary character of the remains of gigantic land-animals embedded in it. … The remains of these nine great quadrupeds, and many detached bones, were found embedded on the beach, within the space of about 200 yards square. It is a remarkable circumstance that so many different species should be found together; and it proves how numerous in kind the ancient inhabitants of this country must have been.
text_zh: 在蓬塔阿尔塔，我们看到其中一片较晚形成的小平原的剖面；里面埋藏的巨型陆地动物遗骸数量之多、形态之奇特，极其引人入胜。……这九种巨大四足兽的遗骸，加上许多零散的骨头，都埋在海滩上约两百码见方的范围内。这么多不同的物种出现在一处，实在不同寻常；它证明这片土地上古时的居民曾经多么繁多。

location: Chapter 4, Rio Negro to Bahia Blanca
location_zh: 第 4 章《从内格罗河到巴伊亚布兰卡》
text_en: The town is indifferently called El Carmen or Patagones. It is built on the face of a cliff which fronts the river, and many of the houses are excavated even in the sandstone. The river is about two or three hundred yards wide, and is deep and rapid. The many islands, with their willow-trees, and the flat headlands, seen one behind the other on the northern boundary of the broad green valley, form, by the aid of a bright sun, a view almost picturesque.
text_zh: 这座镇子既叫埃尔卡门，也叫巴塔哥内斯。它建在临河的一面悬崖上，许多房屋甚至是在砂岩里凿出来的。河宽两三百码，水深流急。河中许多长着柳树的小岛，和宽阔绿色河谷北缘一个接一个的平坦岬角，在明亮的阳光下，构成了一幅近乎如画的景色。

location_zh: 第 21 章《从毛里求斯到英格兰》
text_en: In calling up images of the past, I find that the plains of Patagonia frequently cross before my eyes; yet these plains are pronounced by all wretched and useless. They can be described only by negative characters; without habitations, without water, without trees, without mountains, they support merely a few dwarf plants. Why, then, and the case is not peculiar to myself, have these arid wastes taken so firm a hold on my memory?
text_zh: 回想往事，我发现巴塔哥尼亚的平原常常从眼前掠过；可人人都说这些平原荒凉无用。它们只能用否定的词来描述：没有人家，没有水，没有树，没有山，只长着几株矮小的植物。那么，为什么这些干旱的荒原会如此牢固地占据我的记忆？——而且有这种感受的并不只我一个人。

text_en: This channel, which was discovered by Captain Fitz Roy during the last voyage, is a most remarkable feature in the geography of this, or indeed of any other country: it may be compared to the valley of Lochness in Scotland, with its chain of lakes and friths. … is throughout the greater part so perfectly straight, that the view, bounded on each side by a line of mountains, gradually becomes indistinct in the long distance.
text_zh: 这条水道是菲茨罗伊船长在上一次航行中发现的，在这个国家、甚至在任何国家的地理中，都是极其奇特的一景：它可以和苏格兰的尼斯湖谷相比，也有一连串湖泊和峡湾。……它大部分河段笔直得出奇，两侧各有一列山峦夹住视线，景色在远方渐渐模糊。

location_zh: 第 15 章《翻越科迪勒拉山》
text_en: I saw the spot where a cluster of fine trees once waved their branches on the shores of the Atlantic, when that ocean (now driven back 700 miles) came to the foot of the Andes. I saw that they had sprung from a volcanic soil which had been raised above the level of the sea, and that subsequently this dry land, with its upright trees, had been let down into the depths of the ocean.
text_zh: 我看到了这样一个地方：曾有一丛美丽的树在大西洋岸边摇曳枝叶，那时大洋（如今已后退七百英里）一直延伸到安第斯山脚下。我看出它们生长在一片升出海面的火山土上；后来，这片干燥的陆地连同直立的树木，又沉入了大洋深处。

location: Chapter 1, Physical Aspect of the Argentine Republic
location_zh: 第 1 章《阿根廷共和国的自然面貌》
text_orig: El mal que aqueja a la República Argentina es la extensión: el desierto la rodea por todas partes, se le insinúa en las entrañas; la soledad, el despoblado sin una habitación humana, son por lo general los límites incuestionables entre unas y otras provincias. Allí la inmensidad por todas partes: inmensa la llanura, inmensos los bosques, inmensos los ríos, el horizonte siempre incierto, siempre confundiéndose con la tierra entre celajes y vapores tenues que no dejan en la lejana perspectiva señalar el punto en que el mundo acaba y principia el cielo.
text_en: The evil that afflicts the Argentine Republic is its vastness: the desert surrounds it on every side and works its way into its very heart; solitude, empty land without a single human dwelling, is as a rule the unquestioned border between one province and the next. There, immensity is everywhere: immense the plain, immense the forests, immense the rivers, the horizon always uncertain, always melting into the earth among clouds and thin haze, so that in the far distance no one can mark the point where the world ends and the sky begins.
text_zh: 折磨阿根廷共和国的病，是它的辽阔：荒漠四面包围着它，一直渗进它的腹地；孤寂、不见一户人家的旷野，通常就是这个省和那个省之间无可争议的边界。那里处处都是无边无际：无边的平原，无边的森林，无边的河流；地平线永远模糊不定，总在云霞和薄雾之间与大地混成一片，望向远方，谁也指不出世界在哪里结束、天空从哪里开始。

text_orig:
Y cuando la habían pasao,
una madrugada clara
le dijo Cruz que mirara
las últimas poblaciones,
y a Fierro dos lagrimones
le rodaron por la cara.

Y siguiendo el fiel del rumbo
se entraron en el desierto,
no sé si los habrán muerto
en alguna correría,
pero espero que algún día
sabré de ellos algo cierto.
text_en:
And once they had crossed it,
one clear daybreak
Cruz told him to look back
at the last settlements,
and two big tears
rolled down Fierro's face.

And holding a steady course
they rode into the desert.
I don't know if they were killed
in some raid,
but I hope that one day
I'll hear some sure news of them.
text_zh:
等他们越过了边界，
一个晴朗的黎明，
克鲁斯叫他回头看看
那最后的村落，
两大颗泪珠
顺着菲耶罗的脸颊滚落。

他们认准方向一直走，
走进了荒漠；
不知他们是否已死在
哪一次袭击里，
但愿有一天
我能听到他们确切的消息。

text_en: The house where I was born, on the South American pampas, was quaintly named Los Veinte-cinco Ombues, which means "The Twenty-five Ombu Trees," there being just twenty-five of these indigenous trees-- gigantic in size, and standing wide apart in a row about 400 yards long. … Our trees were about a century old and very large, and, as they stood on an elevation, they could be easily seen at a distance of ten miles.
text_zh: 我出生的那座房子在南美的潘帕斯草原上，名字很别致，叫“二十五棵翁布树”，因为那里正好有二十五棵这种本地树——树身巨大，彼此隔得很开，排成大约四百码长的一行。……我们的树都有一百来岁，非常高大，又长在一片高地上，十英里外就能望见。

text_orig: El Paraná corre allí en el fondo de una inmensa hoya, cuyas paredes, altas de cien metros, encajonan fúnebremente el río. Desde las orillas bordeadas de negros bloques de basalto, asciende el bosque, negro también. Adelante, a los costados, detrás, la eterna muralla lúgubre, en cuyo fondo el río arremolinado se precipita en incesantes borbollones de agua fangosa. El paisaje es agresivo, y reina en él un silencio de muerte. Al atardecer, sin embargo, su belleza sombría y calma cobra una majestad única.
text_en: There the Paraná runs at the bottom of an immense basin whose walls, a hundred metres high, hem the river in like a tomb. From the banks, lined with black blocks of basalt, the forest climbs upward, black as well. Ahead, on either side, behind, the endless gloomy wall, and at its foot the river rushing on in whirlpools and ceaseless surges of muddy water. The landscape is hostile, and a deathly silence reigns over it. At dusk, though, its dark, calm beauty takes on a majesty all its own.
text_zh: 巴拉那河在那里流过一道巨大深谷的谷底，百米高的崖壁像墓穴一样把河夹在中间。两岸堆满黑色的玄武岩块，森林从岸边向上攀去，也是黑的。前面、两旁、身后，都是那道没有尽头的阴森石墙，墙脚下，河水打着漩涡，翻起一股又一股泥浆，奔流不息。这片风景充满敌意，笼罩着死一般的寂静。可到了黄昏，它那阴郁而平静的美，却显出一种独有的庄严。

text_orig: El de San Ignacio, en las Misiones argentinas, revela algo muy semejante: columnas góticas, sobre las cuales se asienta un dintel recargadísimo, pues la blandura del gres predisponía á abundar en decoraciones. Éstas eran muy variadas: el follaje mixto de los capiteles compuestos, los racimos de la viña evangélica; cuartos y medios boceles, golas, cheurrones, escudos encartuchados y angelotes.
text_en: The portico of San Ignacio, in the Argentine Missions, shows something very similar: Gothic columns carrying a heavily laden lintel, for the softness of the sandstone invited a wealth of ornament. The ornament was richly varied: the mixed foliage of composite capitals, the grape clusters of the gospel vine; quarter and half rounds, ogees, chevrons, cartouche shields and cherubs.
text_zh: 阿根廷米西奥内斯的圣伊格纳西奥，门廊也是相近的样子：哥特式的柱子托着一道装饰繁复的门楣——砂岩质地松软，正好让人尽情雕琢。纹样极其多样：复合柱头上交错的枝叶，福音葡萄藤上的串串果实，四分之一圆和半圆的线脚、波纹线脚、人字纹、涡卷盾徽和小天使。

text_en: In Buenos Aires, Rivière, head of the airmail company, waits through the night for three mail planes coming in from Patagonia, Chile and Paraguay, while his pilot Fabien flies into a storm over Patagonia from which he will not return.
text_zh: 在布宜诺斯艾利斯，航空邮政公司的负责人里维埃彻夜等候从巴塔哥尼亚、智利和巴拉圭飞回的三架邮机；他的飞行员法比安却在巴塔哥尼亚上空闯进了一场再也飞不出来的风暴。

text_en: The new lighthouse on Staten Island at the tip of South America has barely been lit when a band of wreckers led by Kongre lands on the island; two of the three keepers are killed, and Vasquez, the last, hides among the rocks and watches the pirates put out the light.
text_zh: 南美洲最南端的埃斯塔多斯岛上，新灯塔刚刚点亮，孔格雷带领的一伙劫船海盗就登上了小岛；三名守塔人死了两个，最后的瓦斯克斯躲在岩石间，眼看着海盗熄灭了灯火。

text_en: On a Saturday in May 1953, a tall, stooping young man named Martín is sitting on a bench by a statue in Parque Lezama when he feels that someone is watching him; it is Alejandra, and she will change his life.
text_zh: 1953 年 5 月的一个星期六，高个子、有点驼背的青年马丁坐在莱萨马公园一座雕像旁的长椅上，忽然觉得有人在看他——那是亚历杭德拉，她将改变他的一生。
